messages:
maya: quick q — when a request with mixed dims (e.g. [1536, 1024]) hits /v1/embeddings do we route by bytes or by dim-slot? i just observed some 413s in staging

sam: currently we route based on total payload bytes (ingress size). dim-aware routing is on the roadmap but not the default. 413s come from per-route max payload enforcement.

kelly: console shows a "per-tenant softcap" but it doesn't surface how to split by dim. UX ask: we should show a suggested split plan when a request would be rejected.

jordan: telemetry note: ~70% of 413s last week were from a handful of mobile SDKs sending base64 arrays (no gzip). we could detect that pattern and suggest gzip + split hints.

maya: for Dedicated customers we already have dim-affinity pools, right? could we prefer dim-aware routing there to avoid cross-shard splits?

sam: yes, dedicated pools have dim-affinity if the request includes X-Embed-Dims header (comma list). otherwise runtime falls back to bytes routing to keep contract simple.

maya: proposal: 1) add server-side autodetect of dims from payload (best-effort) 2) return a preflight endpoint that returns a suggested split plan + estimate, and 3) have console show the suggestion inline.

jordan: +1. metrics to add: embed.preflight.hint_requested, embed.preflight.hint_served, embed.split_applied, and embed.split_latency_delta. also log original vs post-split token counts for quality analysis.

reliability-bot: deploy queued: eng-platform/preflight-hint v2 -> staging :rocket:

kelly: small privacy concern: suggested split plans leak request shape distribution if we show aggregated examples in console. need to sanitize and sample. check privacy/compliance before exposing per-tenant hints publicly.

maya: agree. make hints opt-in and sampled by default. canary behind a feature-flag for enterprise tenants.

sam: runtime change is small: accept header X-Embed-Dims OR run a quick dim-detect pass (O(n)) to decide routing. fallback remains bytes-based. will open PR.

jordan: can we make the preflight endpoint cheap? it needs to be constant-time-ish and not do heavy batching. maybe a quick estimator that returns: { "would_split": true, "split_plan": [1000,1000], "expected_latency_ms": 85 }.

maya: exactly. not a full compile/run. just an estimator. console will call it synchronously and present a non-blocking suggestion.

sam: note on quotas: if we return a split_plan, should we charge full request bytes or per-fragment bytes? my vote: charge based on actual served fragments (post-split) but count toward softcap the original request size for throttling. avoids evasion while reflecting cost.

kelly: UX: console should show "estimated cost change" and a quick toggle to auto-apply split on client SDKs. but default to manual.

jordan: add integration test in client-sdk for mixeddim fastfail flag and preflight hint. flaky path we saw yesterday should be covered.

maya: follow-ups / owners: sam -> runtime PR for header + detector; kelly -> console tile + opt-in toggle; jordan -> telemetry metrics + SDK test; maya -> coordinate privacy review and canary rollout.

sam: i'll add a panel to the embeddings-routing dashboard: preflight.hit_rate, split.applied_rate, post_split_latency_delta.avg.

kelly: i'll draft console copy and a small mock for the hint UI.

maya: timeline: aim for canary next Tue, full rollout the week after if no regression.

jordan: :+1: will prepare dashboards and alerts.

maya: thanks all, will create GH issues and link them here. :eyes:
